The task: write English uninstaller strings following the UI microcopy skill doctrine.

Let me think about each string:

s1: title of dialog asking whether to uninstall. Dialog title should name the act, noun or verb phrase, no question mark. So "Uninstall" is too bare maybe; something like "Uninstall App" or "Uninstall {AppName}". The convention: a dialog title that names the act. In English, e.g., "Uninstall App" — noun phrase naming the act. Not "Are you sure you want to uninstall?" That's a question mark violation. So "Uninstall App Name" or "Uninstall". Since it's a desktop app's uninstaller, generic: "Uninstall App"? Perhaps "Uninstall" is the title convention (macOS uninstaller dialogs often just "Uninstall"). The role form says noun or verb phrase naming the act — "Uninstall App" works. Without an app name, use a placeholder? The task says provide the strings; maybe generic without app name. I could use "Uninstall" — concise. But a dialog body typically carries the consequence; the title alone might be "Uninstall". Hmm, mainstream: Windows UAC is "Uninstall an application"? Actually typical uninstall prompt: title "Uninstall App" body "This will remove the app and its settings." But s1 is just the title, no body requested.

I'll go with "Uninstall App"? Or generic placeholder "[AppName]"? The strings are for a desktop app's uninstaller; likely they'd templated with app name. But safest: "Uninstall" as the title naming the act, no question mark. Actually many uninstallers (e.g., Inno Setup) default: "Do you want to completely remove X?" — but that violates doctrine. Doctrine: dialog-title names the act, noun or verb phrase, no question mark. So "Uninstall App" or "Uninstall". I'll use "Uninstall" — shortest conventional wording. Hmm, but a bare "Uninstall" could collide with button s2 also "Uninstall". That duplication is fine actually (title and button often match), but maybe title "Uninstall App" to differentiate. Without app name, "Uninstall App" reads slightly off. Using a placeholder like "{App}" might be helpful: "Uninstall {App}". I think giving placeholder is reasonable for a real app. But instructions: return only JSON with the strings. I could write "Uninstall App" or "Uninstall {app}". Hmm.

Let me decide: s1 = "Uninstall App". Actually maybe better "Uninstall" — the dialog title. Doctrine example: dialog-title accepted 「刪除這筆紀錄」 (delete this record), rejected question forms. English equivalent: "Delete Record". So "Uninstall App" parallels. I'll go with "Uninstall App".

s2: button that performs uninstall: imperative verb, conventional: "Uninstall". Keep conventional action labels. Yes "Uninstall".

s3: button that keeps the app: this is declining/cancelling. The action: keeps the app, i.e., cancels the uninstall. Label: "Cancel". Per doctrine, cancel button labelled Cancel. Not "Keep App", not "No thanks". The control sits on a dialog asking whether to uninstall; cancel closes without uninstalling. So "Cancel".

s4: status while files are being removed: in-progress state: "Removing files…" or "Uninstalling…". Closed form: 無法+動詞、動詞+中 — English equivalent: "Uninstalling…" The convention: "Removing files…"? The status line shown while files are being removed — "Removing files…" is specific and conventional. Or "Uninstalling…" is more general. The status should name the state: "Uninstalling…" Hmm, doctrine examples: 同步中 = syncing/“Syncing…”. So "Removing files…". Both fine. "Removing files…" describes exactly, matches "files are being removed" prompt. I'll pick "Removing files…". Note ellipsis: use "…" (single character) — fine.

s5: error when uninstall fails because app still running; tell user what to do. Error form: state, cause, recovery step. English: "Uninstall failed: {App} is still running. Close it and try again." But is "Uninstall failed" needed or just "Uninstallation failed"? Conventional: "Uninstallation failed". Hmm. State then cause then recovery: "Uninstall failed: the app is still running. Quit the app, then try again." Should we include "Quit {App} and try again."? One sentence recovery: "Quit the app and try again." Keep concise. Use "try again" — that's a recovery action the user can take, so allowed.

Maybe: "Can't uninstall: the app is still running. Quit it and try again." Doctrine example: 「無法安裝：這是目前的開機磁碟。請選擇其他磁碟。」 = "Can't install: this is the current boot disk. Choose another disk." So English parallel: "Can't uninstall: the app is still running. Quit the app, then try again." Hmm "Can't" vs "Cannot" vs "Uninstall failed". Windows convention often "Installation failed". I think "Uninstall failed: {App} is still running. Quit {App} and try again." Using app reference. Since no app name given, use "the app". Slightly awkward "the app is still running. Quit it and try again." Cleaner: "Uninstall failed: the app is still running. Quit it, then try again." Hmm.

Let me write: "Uninstall failed: the app is still running. Quit the app and try again." Slight repetition of "the app". Could be "Uninstall failed: the app is still running. Quit it and try again." "Quit it" fine. Or "Close the app and try again." I'll go: "Uninstall failed: the app is still running. Quit the app and try again." Hmm repetition—maybe fine, but deletion test: "Quit it and try again." Fine.

Consider affect: no apologies, no "Oops". Good.

JSON escaping: ellipsis character "…" fine in JSON.

Also s4 period? Buttons/labels no period; sentence-type status with period. "Removing files…" uses ellipsis, conventional for in-progress status. Good.
